what_this_is: The teardown record. Captured as late as possible, with this workstation (471041) still alive because destroying it ends execution and therefore must be last.

api.discovery_note: the working family was found because POST /templates/vm/pause answered with a FastAPI validation error naming machine_id as a required QUERY parameter - a 422 was more informative than any of the 404s. Also: /templates/vm/destroy returned a generic 'Something Went wrong' message for the driver and yet the destroy DID take effect, so its error text cannot be trusted as a failure signal.

sequence_and_why.why: the 512k arm was at 43 of 47 with roughly 16 minutes of runway at the full $18.13/hr. Pausing the expensive host cut burn to about $3/hr and converted 16 minutes into ~1.4 hours of closeout time. Four more tasks were worth far less than the ability to finish the receipts, the gap review and the teardown properly.
its artifacts had already been swept twice and the second sweep was verified against the manifest

sequence_and_why.status: LAST - ends execution, so it follows this receipt being pushed

persistence.verified_twice: once before the 512k arm and once after it, so the invariant held AT teardown rather than only at first sweep
persistence.secret_filter: the second sweep was rejected by GitHub push protection for a Hugging Face token inside the sanitize-git-repo task's transcript; 767 files were scanned across seven patterns, 121 fixture matches were found in 2 files, ZERO matches for our own credentials, and both files were deleted rather than allow-listed
